reuse.why: Builds on the existing shared applyWeekendRule/WeekendRule and exports a shared isSkippedWeekendOccurrence used by the budget template and upcoming dates, though getNextDate and getUpcomingDates still compute their own skip/lookahead conditions.

duplication.why: getUpcomingDates re-derives the daily-skip predicate inline (`config.skipWeekend && config.frequency === 'daily'`) and getNextDate uses its own `!d.isWeekend` find, so the rule's condition is spelled in more than one place with two different lookahead heuristics.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside applyWeekendRule, with frequency threaded through parseRecurDate; only the take-sizing heuristic leaks into server/schedules/app.ts.

scope.why: All edits serve the daily weekend-skip rule plus targeted tests.

maintainability.why: A maintainer changing which frequencies skip would have to update the private predicate and the inline copy in getUpcomingDates, and reason about three separate lookahead strategies.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates computes `skipsWeekendDays` itself instead of using the shared predicate (isWeekendOccurrenceSkipped, left unexported).

disguised_duplication.where: app.ts getUpcomingDates `skipsWeekendDays = config.skipWeekend && config.frequency === 'daily'` restates shared/schedules.ts isWeekendOccurrenceSkipped under another name.

one_place.where: The rule is defined in shared/schedules.ts (isWeekendOccurrenceSkipped / isSkippedWeekendOccurrence / applyWeekendRule), but getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts re-decides when the rule applies with its own expression.
